text:
support-jordan: Hey @oncall, multiple ACME customers reporting 504s and very high tail latency from hosted inference since ~09:12 UTC. p95 ~12s, some p99s >20s. Creating thread with repro and logs.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-1764123456. Paging eng-ryan.

eng-ryan: looking. can you paste a failing request payload and model/route?

support-jordan: sample request: POST /v1/generate model=rdx-4k-compat seq_len=2048 tokens=~1800 (long documents). customer says errors spike when they send bulk PDF->text requests. Example log snippet:```
client:req_id=acme-9a2
status: 504 Gateway Timeout
backend: hosted-gateway
latency: 12.3s
queue_depth: 1812/2000
batch_size: 32
continuous_batch_wait: 250ms
```

sophie: queue_depth 1812/2000 is the smoking gun. continuous-batcher backlog + a few longseq jobs clogging KV cache. when the queue approaches depth limit we start dropping/early timeouts. did they start a big re-ingest around 09:10?

support-jordan: yes they ran a bulk ingestion at 09:08 that sent ~1800 long requests over 3 minutes.

eng-ryan: quick triage steps I'll run: check pool utilization, recent model hotfixes, and whether adaptive-shed kicked in. also want to see dequeue latency histograms.

leah: striped in metrics: hosted-pool-1 cpu/gpu util ~92%, dequeue p99 shows large tail. KV cache evictions spike at same time. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/d/hosted/pool-1?from=09:00&to=09:30

sophie: mitigation options (short-term):
- route ACME to rdx-4k-lite (lower memory/shorter max-seq) for the ingestion window
- temporarily raise queue_depth_limit for hosted-pool-1 from 2000 -> 3000 (careful: increases memory pressure)
- enable early-reject threshold at 1500 with informative 429 to encourage retry backoff

eng-ryan: doing an immediate small change: scale pool by +2 nodes and flip adaptive-shed to 1500 early-reject. running command:```
# redwoodctl scale pool hosted-pool-1 --add-nodes 2
Applying... OK
# redwoodctl config set hosted-pool-1 adaptive_shed.early_reject_threshold=1500
Applied (will take effect in 12s)
```

oncall-bot: Runbooks triggered: queue-overrun checklist started. Assigned: sophie, ryan.

support-jordan: I told ACME we are investigating and suggested they throttle to 5 rps while we stabilize. they acknowledged. :thumbsup:

leah: after scale + early-reject: queue_depth dropped to ~900 within 40s, 504s subsided. dequeue p99 improved to ~1.6s. KV evictions reduced.

eng-ryan: log after fix:```
client:req_id=acme-9a2
status: 200 OK
latency: 1.8s
queue_depth: 842/3000
batch_size: 16
```

sophie: next steps (post-incident):
- run customer-specific traffic shaping (rate-limits) for bulk ingestion endpoints
- add a guard to detect big long-seq bulk jobs and auto-route to a dedicated batch lane
- evaluate increasing queue depth or adding eviction-friendly quantized variants for longseq workloads
- add a replay test to our CI that simulates large longseq ingestion to verify healthy degradation

eng-ryan: filing a follow-up ticket: RM-1764123456 (postmortem + config changes). assigning to eng-platform and product to discuss guardrails.

support-jordan: ACME relaunched ingestion at 10:05 and reported no errors. Marking customer status: stabilized.

leah: leaving metric annotations and trace links on the incident. will draft a short customer-facing summary for support.

sophie: thanks all. putting a hold for the postmortem meeting tomorrow 11:00 UTC.

support-jordan: closing this slack thread, will paste postmortem link here when available. :white_check_mark:
